pageCache.text:
A happy, nurturing and empowering environment where autistic children shine.
Welcome to Castle Garden School
Castle Garden School is an independent specialist school for autistic children aged five to eleven and is now proud to be in its third academic year.
Situated in the centre of Guildford, the school provides a highly specialised and nurturing educational environment designed to meet the complex needs of its pupils. Since opening to a small number of pupils in June 2023, the school has grown steadily and now supports a full cohort of 32 pupils, all of whom present with a range of communication, sensory, social and learning profiles.
Curriculum
Our curriculum underpins our ethos and aims to ensure that autistic children and young people are given the opportunity to achieve high standards within a supportive community.
Clinical
When children are happy, confident and well equipped to manage the day-to-day challenges of life, they thrive academically.
Take a look around

pageCache.pageTitle: Referrals and admissions - Castle Garden School
pageCache.text:
Home Parents and Carers Referrals and admissions
Referrals and admissions
Castle Garden School accepts referrals from parents and local authorities. We encourage parents to engage in a dialogue with their child’s current school SENCo and/or local authority in the first instance. Typically, we receive referrals from local authorities once an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP) has been agreed.
Upon receiving a referral, leaders will review the paperwork to see if the school is likely to meet the child/young person’s needs. If leaders feel that needs could be met, an initial offer to assess the child/young person is made. All offers to assess are directed to the local authority in the first instance.
Following an assessment, which may take place at the child or young person’s home and/or current school, the team will confirm if Castle Garden School can meet their needs. If the assessment team feel that needs can be met, a visit to the school will be offered. The nature and duration of this visit will be tailored to the needs of each child/young person.
At the end of this process, an offer letter is sent to the local authority with starting dates and fees. Within the first 12 weeks of the child starting at the school, we will arrange for a post admission review to be held. At this meeting, the placement will be discussed and any amendments to the provision agreed with parents/carers and the local authority.
If you’d like to make a referral or you simply want to know more, please don’t hesitate to get in touch.

Home Our Approach Curriculum
Curriculum
We provide a highly adaptable curriculum that meets each child exactly where they are, tailoring learning to their individual needs, strengths, and aspirations. Through personalised pathways, small classes, and a therapeutic, autism friendly environment, we ensure every young person accesses an engaging, meaningful and achievable curriculum that supports their progress and promotes their identity and independence.
We run carousel subjects across 2 days to offer enrichment and access to a wider curriculum. These include PSHE, Forest School. Performing Arts (music, movement and drama), Food Exploration (sensory curiosity around taste, touch and smell), Life Skills in the Kitchen, and Gardening and Horticulture.
Our curriculum is broken down into termly topics, with project-based learning as a way to draw together knowledge and skills in a purposeful outcome. We promote heuristic play, life and independence skills, creativity and enrichments to effectively engage and deliver the curriculum content. Please click on the links below to see our curriculum overview examples. All topics are supported by our whole school assemblies and a wide range of texts and books. Home About Us Meet Our Team
Meet our team
Welcome from the Headteacher
Castle Garden School is a truly special provision, dedicated to creating a supportive, happy, engaging and healthy environment where autistic children can thrive. It is a privilege for both myself and our staff team to be part of shaping a new school that is already growing into a strong, nurturing and ambitious community.
I have worked across multiple specialist education settings, including all-age through schools and a dedicated autistic provision. Before working in specialist education, I taught mathematics and computer science in mainstream secondary schools, following an earlier career in finance and IT. This breadth of experience has shaped my belief in the power of high quality, personalised teaching and strong, multi agency collaboration. It has also strengthened my commitment to building meaningful partnerships between children, families, clinicians, teachers, support staff and external agencies. Effective partnerships are built on trust—rooted in transparency and open communication—and these values sit at the heart of our school.
Safeguarding remains our highest priority, and every decision we make places the child at the centre. We are committed to asking and accepting pupils’ preferences, while supporting them to navigate the world with confidence and independence. Our curriculum is aspirational, enjoyable, broad and balanced — designed to meet pupils where they are, build on their strengths, and enable them to flourish. Our pupils are supported by highly skilled staff with a growth mindset—professionals who continually refine and improve their practice so the school can evolve to meet the needs of the children we serve.
Since becoming the permanent Headteacher in January 2025, I have taken full ownership of the school’s direction. Through reflection, review and a deep understanding of our pupils’ needs, the leadership team and I have shaped a strong Vision and Mission to guide Castle Garden School from a new setting into a confident, established and thriving school.
Our Vision – To open the gateway to the wider world and give children and young people the life skills and knowledge to navigate it.
Our Mission – To inspire engagement through a breadth of experiences and opportunities that promote identity and independence.
Together, we will build a lasting and supportive community at Castle Garden School—one where every child is understood, celebrated and empowered to thrive.

Home About Us What we do
What We Do
Castle Garden School is an independent specialist school for autistic children aged five to eleven and is now proud to be in its third academic year. Situated in the centre of Guildford, the school provides a highly specialised and nurturing educational environment designed to meet the complex needs of its pupils. Since opening to a small number of pupils in June 2023, the school has grown steadily and now supports a full cohort of 32 pupils, all of whom present with a range of communication, sensory, social and learning profiles.
The school delivers personalised teaching and learning within an autism‑specific environment, ensuring that each child’s individual needs, strengths and therapeutic priorities are fully understood and supported. Its curriculum is shaped by pupils’ EHCP outcomes and is underpinned by integrated clinical input, including speech and language therapy, occupational therapy and creative psychotherapy. This enables pupils to make meaningful progress through carefully sequenced Individual Therapeutic and Education Plans (ITEPs) and approaches that prioritise communication, emotional regulation, and readiness for learning.
Castle Garden School offers a unique blend of specialist education, therapy and pastoral support for children across a wide spectrum of need. Many pupils have previously experienced disrupted education or unsuccessful placements, and the school’s highly structured, neuro‑affirming and relationship‑based approach allows them to build confidence, develop positive peer relationships, and re‑engage successfully with learning. In this specialist setting, pupils’ capabilities are recognised, nurtured and celebrated, supporting each child to achieve their full potential both in education and in life.
© Outcomes First Group 2026
